questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That my home university had an agreement with receiving university and therefore the application procedure was easier.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There were some challenges with the registration proces to courses at the beginning but at the end they were cleared out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yes, it was a help of my student coordinator at a receiving university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: an apartment with two seperate rooms, I should choose between. Kitchenette with a hob and a bathroom shared with my flatmate.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: gas stove for two burners in the kitchenette and and a student canteen on the ground floor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
That there were very kind staff that was willing to help in any situation one might come up with.
There is no electric kettle in the apartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were stress in terms of my chosen subject. At the time I arrived I was not sure If I can take up these courses I had chosen and that previously had been approved of my home university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fine. I took quite a lot of time to have everything in place. I will suggest that the time we had to choose courses in april based on an not actual list was way to early and I could not see a point in it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: professional and quick contact with my student coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That they should always contact first with the student coordinator instead of waiting for second round registeration to chosen courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were well thought out and the level was set high but I was not content with few of the courses, where there was a lot of learning by heart insted of critical thinking.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Copenhagen we have 2 or 3 courses and each of them has descreibed a worlload so a student know how much prepering he/she can expect. There is not such a thing like a course workload in Warsaw and the teachers can give students a lot of meterials they should read for the next lesson even though the subject is eqivalent of only 3 ECTS points.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Analysis of Literary Texts, Research Tour, The Cultural History of Psychoanalysis up to 1950, History of Nordic Cultures, History from below, Cult Films, Reading Images, Avant-garde Academy, Jewish Culture in Poland

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Comparative Analysis of Literary Texts - interesting selection of texts
Reasearch Tour - intensive but packed with knowledge tour
History from below - to have focus on less popular narratives of the big events in the history, it opens a new perspective
Reading Images - I realised how importent the visual art is in my education and had a possibility to create a painting on my own
